title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Route Manifest. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. All cards are translated into your pinned light green + grey clay palette and a transport typeface.

options.label: Route Manifest
options.lineage: truck dispatch waybills and CMR consignment notes, with their green carbon copy
options.thesis: Your pickup is a line on tomorrow's truck manifest, and one tap edits the route.
materials: Barlow / Barlow Semi Condensed (DIN-like highway face), tabular figures
options.viewport: A light-green manifest sheet: boxed field 01 'Kitas išvežimas' with the date huge in Barlow Semi Condensed, field 02 the 14-day ledger as an exact ruler, and a live strip 'Rytojaus maršrutas: 145 → 144 sustojimai' that ticks when you skip; history and container are the sheet's side fields.
options.risk: Paperwork can read bureaucratic if the fields are cramped; it needs big type and generous boxes.

raised.raise: Every number is tabular and column-aligned, so dates, stop counts and kg read like a manifest, not prose.
The focused day in the ledger expands its detail while the rest of the strip quiets.
The 14-day ledger is a true ruler: equal day widths, today marked, the 2-week schedule drawn as a span.
Light green owns whole regions (the manifest sheet itself), never just accent dots.
1px hairline rules divide every field; no floating shadow cards anywhere.

options.label: Collection Calendar
options.lineage: the printed yearly 'Atliekų išvežimo grafikas' leaflet / fridge magnet
options.thesis: The fridge-magnet schedule every house already has, made live.
options.viewport: A full year-at-a-glance grid with October open, tomorrow's dot ringed, and skip/book as marks on the grid itself.
options.risk: Familiar: this is where most runs for a scheduling product land, and month grids get dense on mobile.

options.label: Pickup Pass + Route Board
options.lineage: boarding pass and live departure/gate board
options.thesis: Each pickup is a segmented pass; the route board re-ranks in place when a house drops out.
options.viewport: A pass for 'Pn 10-16 · Stotelė 37/145' beside a mini route board where your row slides out when you skip.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and judges know passes instantly; holds audience identification, loses narrowly on clarity because a pass implies travel, not waste.
options.risk: Can read as an airline theme if the pass is decorated instead of functional.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Pickups as a barcode field of bars and numbers.
options.viewport: A strobing bar field of 319 houses.
options.case: Loses both axes: residents do not recognise themselves in a data artwork, and pure black/white overrides your pinned palette.

options.label: Title Card Wall
options.thesis: Days as poster tiles in a horizontal wall.
options.viewport: Rows of day tiles on a dark ground.
options.case: Loses both axes: entertainment framing, dark ground fights the light palette.
options.kept: Focus reveals detail while the rest quiets.

options.label: Time Score
options.thesis: Time as a vertical staff read upward.
options.viewport: A vertical score of the next 14 days.
options.case: Loses both axes: notation nobody can read.
options.kept: Time as an exact spatial ruler.

options.label: Guide Map Lobes
options.thesis: Areas as swelling lobes of flat colour.
options.viewport: The demo street as a green lobe.
options.case: Loses both axes: you ruled out playful.

options.label: Plate Section
options.thesis: Registration crosshairs and hairline credit rows.
options.viewport: A printed plate of the pickup date.
options.case: Loses both axes: design-world in-joke, not a resident tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean utility dashboard: white cards, one accent, system type, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Header, big next-pickup card, calendar card, side cards.
canonCard.risk: Close to what you have now and to what you said feels like generic SaaS.
